question: In which year was Operation Flood started with an aim to create a nationwide milk grid?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1970**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Operation Flood, launched in 1970, was a project of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) of India.
 
• It is also known as the White Revolution of India and is one of the largest dairy development programs in the world.
 
• The initiative transformed India from a milk-deficient nation into the world's largest milk producer.
 
• It was aimed at creating a nationwide milk grid, linking producers with consumers in over 700 towns and cities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)**

 
 
• NDDB was established in 1965 by Dr. Verghese Kurien, who is considered the architect of Operation Flood.
 
• The board aims to promote, finance, and support producer-owned and controlled organizations.
 
 
 
• **White Revolution**
 
 
• The White Revolution refers to the rapid development of the dairy sector in India, primarily due to Operation Flood.
 
• It led to a significant increase in milk production, making India self-sufficient in dairy products.
 
• The revolution also improved rural incomes and provided a sustainable livelihood to millions of small and marginal farmers.
 
 
 
• **Three Phases of Operation Flood**
 
 
• Operation Flood was carried out in three phases: Phase I (1970-1980), Phase II (1981-1985), and Phase III (1985-1996).
 
• Phase I focused on creating milk-sheds and establishing a nationwide milk grid.
 
• Phase II expanded the program to more regions and enhanced milk production and procurement.
 
• Phase III aimed at consolidating gains, improving processing infrastructure, and ensuring the financial viability of dairy cooperatives.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Dairy Farmers**
 
 
• Operation Flood enabled small and marginal farmers to gain access to markets and receive fair prices for their milk.
 
• It also provided technical support, training, and veterinary services to farmers, enhancing their productivity and income.
